_about: Every word a visitor reads lives in this file. Layout and code never contain reader-facing text. {name} markers are filled in by the page.
title: PayCheck Sui
tagline: One agent gets burned. Every other agent is warned.
intro: I built PayCheck so an AI agent can look at a Sui address before it pays. When one agent loses money to an address, that lesson is saved in shared memory. The next agent about to pay a different address from the same group gets stopped, even though it has never seen that address.

bench.columnsHonest: The plain AI also got the same report that memory holds, written into its prompt. It stops about as many group wallets as memory does. So the value here is not smarter reasoning. It is a report that is shared, kept, and read by every agent without being told to look. The small model may be beaten by a stronger one, and you can run it with --model=<name>. Stronger models were over quota or limited to 20 calls a day on my key.
bench.lossesHeading: Where the checker with memory did not do well
bench.lossesLead: Four held-out cases, listed as they are:

losses.text: The AI said "do not pay". The checker said "pay", because the link was a shared fee payer and the report did not reach it.
An ordinary wallet that sent money back to its funder. The checker said "caution", the AI said "pay".
The AI named the recorded funder. The checker did not name it, though memory still stopped the wallet.
The checker found no link, because the shared transactions are not in the oldest 50 it reads. It said "pay".

limits.heading: What this is not, and where it is weak
items: It is not a fraud detector. Being linked to other wallets is not unsafe, because exchanges and payroll wallets fund many honest wallets. A red answer needs a stored report of a bad payment that reaches the address through a real link.
It cannot protect the first wallet in a brand new group. With no report anywhere in the group, the answer is "pay, linked, no bad history" and the links are only shown.
It reads only the oldest 50 transactions of a wallet. On a busy wallet that can hide a link. Two of the 20 real groups were missed, and one of those misses was for this reason.
Shared services are spotted with a rule I chose: 15 or more wallets over 25 hours or more. Those two numbers are my picks. They are checked against real data, not proven.
One bad report is enough to turn a direct link red. The answer always shows who reported it and the memory id, so you can judge the source.
The real set has small groups (2 to 9 wallets) and young control wallets. It shows the method works on real chain data, not that it works everywhere.
Ankr's history for an address is shallower than Tatum's, so some links are checked by transaction instead of by address history.

footer: PayCheck Sui, built for the Tatum and Walrus Memory hackathon. Sui data through Tatum, cross-checked with Ankr, memory in Walrus Memory.
